property.title: Coefficient-array bounds safety over the full 256-iteration loop
property.candidate_statement: The loop in mlk_poly_add iterates i from 0 to MLKEM_N-1 with MLKEM_N = 256, so a candidate CBMC harness can check that r->coeffs[i] and b->coeffs[i] are always accessed within the declared coefficient array bounds for all iterations.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: for (i = 0; i < MLKEM_N; i++) ... r->coeffs[i] = (int16_t)(r->coeffs[i] + b->coeffs[i]);
supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The loop covers the full 256-element coefficient range and indexes both operands coefficient-wise.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: typedef struct { int16_t coeffs[MLKEM_N]; } MLK_ALIGN mlk_poly; ... requires(memory_no_alias(r, sizeof(mlk_poly))) ... requires(memory_no_alias(b, sizeof(mlk_poly)))
supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The coefficient storage is a fixed-size MLKEM_N-element array and the function expects distinct valid objects.

required_assumptions: The harness should use the configured build where MLKEM_N resolves to 256.
r and b must each point to valid mlk_poly objects with at least MLKEM_N coefficients accessible.
The harness should model r and b as distinct fresh objects or otherwise justify non-aliasing using the repository's CBMC memory model.
property.expected_artifact_type: Bounded-loop CBMC harness with explicit pointer validity assumptions and coefficient-index safety assertions
out_of_scope_boundaries: Do not extend this into claims about polynomial multiplication, NTT correctness, or serialization size.
Do not infer anything about coefficient value ranges beyond index safety from this property alone.
Do not claim modular reduction or canonical [0,q-1] normalization for mlk_poly_add; the source routine performs plain in-place signed addition with overflow-preventing preconditions.
property.uncertainty: Index safety is directly supported by the fixed-size type and the simple loop bound. The harness still depends on valid object allocation and the CBMC configuration matching the provided headers.
limitations: This property checks access safety, not arithmetic correctness.
It is a local property of mlk_poly_add only.
The property is intentionally narrower than the FIPS coordinate-wise modular semantics, because the C implementation is a signed int16_t accumulator without reduction.

parsed_json.intended_check: Check that the harness can non-vacuously model two distinct mlk_poly objects, call mlk_poly_add exactly once, and expose the coefficient indexing pattern over the full MLKEM_N = 256 range without out-of-bounds access.
non_goals: Do not prove full ML-KEM correctness.
Do not prove cryptographic security or side-channel resistance.
Do not prove modular normalization to canonical representatives.
Do not prove caller-side preconditions beyond the local harness assumptions.

assumption_plan.assumption: r and b are valid, distinct mlk_poly objects satisfying the memory_no_alias-style non-aliasing requirement.
assumption_plan.justification: The header contract explicitly requires memory_no_alias for both pointers, and the implementation comment states the destructive form was chosen to avoid aliasing reasoning.

assumption_plan.assumption: For every coefficient index k in [0, MLKEM_N), the signed addition is within the int16_t range.
assumption_plan.justification: The header explicitly requires this to avoid undefined behavior, and the body comment states that the preconditions imply int16_t safety.

assumption_plan.assumption: The candidate property is scoped to the C-level semantics of mlk_poly_add rather than the mathematical modular semantics of R_q / T_q addition.
assumption_plan.justification: The source function performs plain int16_t addition without modular reduction; conflating it with modular arithmetic would contradict the implementation.

evidence_references.excerpt: The coefficients of @p r and @p b must be such that the addition does not overflow. Otherwise, the behaviour of this function is undefined.

old_state_snapshot_plan.reason: The selected property is array-bounds safety, which does not inherently require a pre-state snapshot for its core obligation. However, because the function mutates r in place and the repository contract uses old(*r) / loop_entry(*r), an explicit old-state snapshot is still advisable if any future post-call relation is added or if the generated harness is later extended to check the contract-style relation.
snapshot_items: pre_r_coeffs[0..MLKEM_N-1] copied from r->coeffs before the call
optionally pre_b_coeffs[0..MLKEM_N-1] if a frame check for b is later added

disagreements.deterministic_claim: The harness should be centered on coefficient-array bounds safety with a simple bounded loop and concrete object modeling.
disagreements.primary_evidence_finding: The source supports coefficient-wise in-place addition over a 256-element array, but the actual function contract also includes non-aliasing and overflow-preventing preconditions; a bounds-only harness must not overstate arithmetic or modular guarantees.
disagreements.resolution: Kept the bounds-safety property, but made the plan explicit that it is local, does not assert modular normalization, and models the objects concretely without relying on vacuous null pointers.
